newsitem.title: USA: Unhappy Digital shareholders to meet- paper.
newsitem.headline: Unhappy Digital shareholders to meet- paper.

text.p: A shareholder activist will meet with institutional shareholders of Digital Equipment Corp who are disappointed with the company's performance, the Boston Globe reported Thursday.

Herbert Denton, head of the broker-dealer Providence Capital Inc, holds a small amount of stock, but the meeting will gather the owners of an estimated 40 percent of Digital's outstanding stock, he told the newspaper. The meeting is scheduled for June 18 in New York.
A Digital spokesman said the company's management would not be at the meeting, the Globe reported.
"We're not satisfied with our performance," spokesman Dan Kaferle told the Globe. "We know we can do a lot better and we are going to do a lot better."
Denton said, "This is a company that has lost billions of dollars in the last five or six years. It is quite appropriate that critical questions be raised."
"We've talked to the top 15 shareholders and the vast majority have indicated an interest in attending," he said.
None of the largest shareholders the newspaper contacted would comment.
Denton has taken on management at other companies before, including California Microwave Inc and Ashland Inc and is in a current battle with Comsat Corp, according to the Globe.
Denton said he will take a "kinder, softer approach" with Digital and the June meeting will be geared toward asking questions, the Globe said.
